Java.description: A strongly typed, object-oriented language widely used for backend services, Android development, and enterprise software.
concepts: Declare values with types such as int, double, boolean, and String. Local variables must be initialized before use.
Use if/else, switch, for, while, and enhanced for loops to control execution.
Methods package reusable behavior. Parameters and return types are declared explicitly.
Arrays have a fixed length. String is immutable; StringBuilder is useful for repeated modifications.
Classes, objects, encapsulation, inheritance, abstraction, interfaces, and polymorphism form Java's OOP foundation.
List, Set, Map, and Queue interfaces provide common data structures. ArrayList and HashMap are frequently used.
Use try/catch/finally and throw/throws to handle exceptional conditions.
Generics provide compile-time type safety for reusable classes and methods.
Streams support declarative collection processing; lambdas represent functional interfaces.
Use java.nio.file and java.io APIs for files, paths, and streams.
dictionary: Java Virtual Machine; runs Java bytecode.
Java Development Kit; includes tools for developing Java programs.
Java Runtime Environment; runtime libraries and JVM conceptually needed to run Java apps.
A blueprint that defines state and behavior.
A mechanism for deriving a class from another class.
One interface or parent type can refer to different implementations.
Keeping state and behavior together while controlling access.
A contract that classes can implement.
An event that disrupts normal program flow.

Python.description: A readable, general-purpose language popular for automation, data science, AI, scripting, and interviews.
concepts: Names refer to objects; common types include int, float, bool, str, list, tuple, set, and dict.
Use if/elif/else, for, while, break, and continue.
Define functions with def; default parameters, keyword arguments, *args, and **kwargs help create flexible APIs.
Lists are mutable sequences, tuples are immutable sequences, sets hold unique values, and dictionaries map keys to values.
List/dict/set comprehensions express collection transformations concisely.
Strings are immutable sequences of Unicode characters; slicing supports concise substring operations.
Classes define attributes and methods; inheritance and special methods support reusable designs.
Use try/except/else/finally and raise to manage errors.
Import reusable code from modules and organize larger projects into packages.
Iterators produce values sequentially; yield creates generator functions.
dictionary: Key-value mapping, commonly written with braces.
An object whose state can change.
An object that can produce its members one at a time.
An iterator commonly created using yield.
The widely used Python style guide.
Python's value representing absence of a value.
A callable that wraps or modifies another callable's behavior.

JavaScript.description: The core language of the web, used in browsers, servers, and full-stack applications.
concepts: Use const by default and let when reassignment is needed; avoid var in modern code.
JavaScript has primitive values and objects; use strict equality === to avoid many coercion surprises.
Functions can be declarations, expressions, or arrow functions; they are first-class values.
Arrays store ordered values; objects store properties and methods.
The Document Object Model lets browser JavaScript query and update page elements.
Event listeners respond to clicks, keyboard input, form submissions, and other events.
Promises represent future completion or failure; async/await makes asynchronous code easier to read.
Use export and import to organize code across modules.
A closure retains access to its lexical scope after the outer function returns.
Use try/catch and throw; handle rejected promises appropriately.
dictionary: Document Object Model; a structured representation of a web page.
A function together with its preserved lexical environment.
JavaScript's declaration processing behavior before execution.
An object representing eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation.
A function passed to another function for later invocation.
An event propagating from a target toward ancestor elements.
A text format for exchanging structured data.
A special numeric value meaning Not-a-Number.
The region where an identifier is accessible.
A defined interface through which software components communicate.

C.description: A procedural systems language that teaches memory, pointers, compilation, and low-level programming.
concepts: Include headers and define main; main typically returns an integer status code.
Use int, char, float, double, and carefully chosen types for values.
Use if/else, switch, for, while, and do-while.
Declare and define functions with parameter and return types.
C strings are null-terminated character arrays; prevent buffer overflows.
Pointers store addresses. Understand dereferencing, pointer arithmetic, and NULL.
Use malloc/calloc/realloc and free carefully when dynamic allocation is needed.
struct groups related fields into one custom type.
Use FILE pointers and functions such as fopen, fgets, fprintf, and fclose.
Macros and #include directives are processed before compilation.
dictionary: A variable that stores a memory address.
Access the value at a pointer's address using *.
A contiguous sequence of elements of the same type.
A common runtime failure from invalid memory access.
A file commonly containing declarations and macros.
Program behavior for which the C standard imposes no requirements.
Memory commonly used for call frames and automatic local storage.
Memory region used for dynamic allocation.
A program that translates source code into another representation, often machine code.

C++.description: A high-performance language supporting procedural, object-oriented, and generic programming.
concepts: Use built-in types, conditions, loops, and functions.
References alias objects; pointers hold addresses and may be null.
Classes bundle state and behavior; RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime.
vector, string, map, unordered_map, set, queue, and stack solve common problems.
Use standard algorithms such as sort, find, and lower_bound.
Templates enable generic functions and classes.
Prefer standard containers and smart pointers over manual new/delete in most application code.
Move operations can transfer resources instead of copying them.
Use try/catch and standard exception types when appropriate.
Learn auto, range-for, lambdas, smart pointers, and optional.
dictionary: Standard Template Library, including containers, iterators, and algorithms.
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization; resource lifetime follows object lifetime.
A compile-time mechanism for generic code.
An alias to an existing object.
A dynamically sized contiguous sequence container.
An abstraction for traversing a container.
An object that manages a dynamically allocated object's lifetime.
A named scope used to organize identifiers.
Using the same function/operator name with different signatures or meanings.
Behavior for which the language standard provides no requirements.

C#.description: A modern language on .NET used for web, desktop, cloud, and game development.
concepts: Learn value types, reference types, var, nullable values, and type conversion.
Use conditions, loops, pattern matching, and switch expressions.
Methods can have overloads, optional parameters, and named arguments.
Classes model reference objects; records are useful for data-centric models.
Use interfaces and inheritance to define contracts and shared behavior.
Lists, dictionaries, and LINQ support expressive data processing.
Use try/catch/finally and throw for exceptional cases.
Write asynchronous operations without blocking the calling thread.
Create reusable, type-safe methods and types.
Use .NET libraries for files, HTTP, JSON, and application development.
dictionary: Common Language Runtime, which executes .NET managed code.
Language Integrated Query for querying collections and data sources.
The .NET package manager and package ecosystem.
A contract describing members that implementing types provide.
A type-safe reference to a method.
A type designed for data-oriented modeling and value-based equality.
A logical grouping of related types.
Automatic reclamation of unreachable managed objects.
A type or annotation representing that a value may be absent.

Go.description: A compiled language known for simple syntax, concurrency support, and cloud infrastructure tooling.
concepts: Every Go source file belongs to a package; executable programs use package main.
Use var or := for declarations; Go is statically typed.
Functions can return multiple values, commonly an error alongside a result.
Slices are flexible views over arrays; maps store key-value pairs.
Structs group fields; methods attach behavior to a receiver type.
Interfaces describe behavior through method sets and are implemented implicitly.
Errors are values; handle returned errors explicitly.
Goroutines are lightweight concurrent execution units.
The testing package supports automated tests with go test.
dictionary: A typed conduit used to communicate between goroutines.
A dynamically sized descriptor over an underlying array.
The default value for a variable declared without explicit initialization.
A set of method signatures that a type can satisfy implicitly.
Schedules a function call to run when the surrounding function returns.
A collection of Go packages versioned as a unit.
A timing-dependent bug involving concurrent access.
A value representing an operation's failure.

Rust.description: A systems language focused on performance and memory safety without a garbage collector.
concepts: Bindings are immutable by default; use mut for mutable bindings.
Each value has an owner; ownership rules help prevent memory errors.
References allow access without taking ownership; borrowing rules constrain aliases.
Structs model records and enums model one-of-many variants.
match and if let handle enum variants and structured values.
Option models presence/absence; Result models success or error.
Traits define shared behavior and enable generic constraints.
Lifetime annotations describe reference relationships when needed.
Vec, String, HashMap, and iterators are core tools.
Cargo builds projects, manages dependencies, and runs tests.
dictionary: The rule determining which binding owns a value.
Using a reference to a value without taking ownership.
The scope over which a reference is valid.
A definition of behavior that types can implement.
A type that can represent one of several variants.
An enum representing Some(value) or None.
An enum representing Ok(value) or Err(error).
Rust's build tool and package manager.
Selecting behavior based on a value's structure.

Ruby.description: A dynamic, expressive language known for developer-friendly syntax and web development.
concepts: Variables do not require explicit type declarations.
Arrays and hashes are central data structures.
Methods define reusable behavior; blocks, procs, and lambdas support callbacks.
Use if/unless, case, while, and iterators such as each.
Classes model objects; modules provide namespaces and mixins.
Enumerable methods such as map, select, and reduce simplify collection processing.
Symbols are immutable identifiers often used as hash keys.
Use File and IO APIs to read and write files.
Minitest and RSpec are common testing options.
dictionary: An immutable identifier commonly used as a hash key.
A chunk of code passed to a method.
Behavior included from a module into a class.
A module providing collection iteration methods.
Ruby's object representing absence of a value.
An object's suitability is based on behavior it supports.
An object that stores a block for later execution.
A popular Ruby web application framework.
An object representing an exceptional condition.

PHP.description: A server-side scripting language widely used for web applications and content management systems.
concepts: Variables begin with $; PHP supports scalar, array, object, and other types.
Use if/else, switch, for, foreach, while, and do-while.
Define reusable functions with function and optionally declare parameter/return types.
PHP arrays act as ordered maps and can be indexed or associative.
Use interpolation, concatenation with dot, and standard string functions.
Classes support properties, methods, inheritance, interfaces, and traits.
Validate input and understand request methods and response handling.
Use PDO or database-specific extensions with parameterized queries.
Escape output, validate input, protect sessions, and use prepared SQL statements.
dictionary: PHP Data Objects, a consistent database access interface.
An array whose keys are named or otherwise non-sequential.
Server-side state associated with a user across requests.
A reusable set of methods for classes.
A way to organize PHP identifiers and avoid naming conflicts.
A parameterized database query that separates SQL structure from values.
Cross-site scripting, where untrusted content executes as script.
Cross-site request forgery, an attack that tricks a browser into making unwanted requests.

SQL.description: A language for querying and managing relational databases; this runner may not support SQL execution on every online compiler service.
concepts: Choose columns or expressions from tables.
Aggregate rows by one or more expressions.
Filter grouped results, often using aggregates.
Combine rows from related tables using join conditions.
Use a query inside another query.
WITH clauses name temporary query results for one statement.
Compute values across related rows without collapsing them into groups.
Indexes can speed up lookups; transactions group operations with ACID properties.
dictionary: Column or columns uniquely identifying a row.
Constraint linking values to a key in another table.
Designing tables to reduce redundancy and update anomalies.
Combines rows from tables based on a relationship.
A data structure that can speed up retrieval at a storage and maintenance cost.
A logical unit of database work.
Represents missing or unknown information, not ordinary zero or empty text.
A function such as COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, or MAX.
A named query presented like a virtual table.
